title: Vetra Studio is a dedicated cloud AI agent driving a four-phase Ideate to Specify to Build to Deploy product cycle
content:
## One provisioned agent per product

Vetra Studio is the browser UI for the **Vetra agent**. Each studio you create is a *dedicated cloud agent* tied to your identity, running in an isolated environment that hosts the agent, its workspace and the preview services, on its own `<slug>.vetra.io` subdomain. Opening it lands you inside Powerhouse Connect at `<slug>.vetra.io/d/<drive-id>` — the Studio is not a separate app but a chat pane bolted onto Connect, with the phase-cycle cards, documents and build preview in the main pane.

Access is gated: log in at vetra.io with a wallet via Renown, open the Products dashboard at `/user`, and either paste an invite code, join the waitlist, or run it locally. With a code, the Anthropic API key powering the agent is supplied behind the code, so there is nothing to enter. Products move `Provisioning… → Ready` before they can be opened. The product is **pre-alpha** — back documents up by download or GitHub at the end of a cycle.

## The four phases

| Phase | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 1 Ideate | Frame problem and audience — problem, audience and brand sheets, a feature, a work breakdown structure |
| 2 Specify | Pin down data model, workflow and states — document models grouped into projects |
| 3 Build | The agent generates and tests code, with a live preview of the running app |
| 4 Deploy | Publish the package and run it in Vetra Cloud environments |

Availability is progress-gated: BUILD shows a preview only after the agent scaffolds a reactor project, and DEPLOY requires a Renown sign-in.

Chat sessions are **CRDT documents stored in the studio's reactor**, so they survive restarts, are shareable by URL (`?session=<id>`), and are scoped per identity — clicking **Authorize agent** switches the studio from a generated `did:key` to your wallet `did:pkh` and therefore changes which sessions the list shows. Agent tool calls stream inline as expandable cards (`spec-create`, `spec-generate`, `reactor-project-init`, `spec-preview-show`, plus workspace Read/Write/Edit).

Note a naming tension in the docs: the Build section describes "Vetra Studio" as the local `ph vetra` builder environment, while GetStarted describes this hosted agent product. Both names are in use.

_Source: `apps/academy/docs/academy/01-GetStarted/00-VetraStudio.md`, Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: Each studio is its own cloud agent on a <slug>.vetra.io subdomain, reached from vetra.io with an early-access code, opening into Connect with a chat pane.
